submitLabel: Your ladder mapping, the AI-use map, and the write-up
intro: Paste your matter type, its work products mapped to the five rungs, the honest map of where AI is already used in your function, your one rung-boundary rule, your predicted share of team AI use scored against what you found, and the 300–400 word write-up. Process and work-product types only — no case facts, names, dates, or paraphrased allegations. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, Labor & Employee Relations track — for ER specialists and investigators, ER centres of excellence, labor relations managers and contract administrators who have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 1 applied activity, 'The ladder, and what's already on it'. OVERRIDING FIRST CHECK, WHICH APPLIES TO EVERY ACTIVITY IN THIS TRACK: no case facts. If the submission contains employee or complainant names, initials, dates of specific incidents, paraphrased allegations, or identifying descriptions such as 'an employee in Finance', stop and say so at the top of your feedback, ask for a resubmission with it removed, and do not reproduce any of it or grade the substance. The track works at the level of process and work-product types precisely because case content must never reach an AI-graded submission, an operator review queue, or the tutor. This is a rejection condition, not a caution. The activity has five parts. (1) One matter type the learner owns end to end — harassment intake, discipline consistency, grievance handling at a step, a bargaining subject — a TYPE, not a case, which the remaining seven modules attach to. (2) The work products that matter type produces, each placed on a rung of the evidentiary ladder: observation (what was said, seen, recorded), corroboration (what other evidence exists, including absences), inference (what it could mean, plural), finding (what you conclude happened, requiring weighing), determination (what follows for a person). Documents that span rungs should be broken down by section, and the spanning documents are the interesting ones because that is where a rung-four sentence hides in a rung-two section. (3) An honest map of where AI is ALREADY used in the function: the rung, the tool, whether it is approved, and whether case content was involved — obtained by asking the team WITHOUT PENALTY, and the submission should say that they asked and how they framed it. 'I don't know' is a valid entry. (4) One rung-boundary sentence they would put in front of their team tomorrow — one sentence, applicable to a sentence in a document, not a policy. (5) The prediction scored. KEY GRADING INSTRUCTIONS: the module's central control is that the rung boundary rather than the task is what governs, because a summary can sit on any rung. So grade the one rule in part 4 on whether it can be applied to an individual SENTENCE — 'AI may help with drafting but not decisions' fails this; 'AI may establish what exists and may never weigh it' passes. AI's permission stops absolutely between inference and finding, and at rung three it may only generate untested plural possibilities, never rank or select. Reward a learner who identified a work product whose grammar suggests one rung and whose content does another — a characterization presented as an observation is the archetype. Reward asking the team without penalty and reporting something unexpected; a submission claiming zero AI use with no evidence of having asked should be gently pushed on, given the benchmark finding that 70% of ER teams used or trialled AI in 2025. Reward identifying rung two as under-used, since the module argues that is where the leverage is. Do not reward a conclusion that AI should be prohibited outright in the function; the module's position is that every control must be cheaper than the workaround or it loses to the workaround. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that unsanctioned AI use here is arithmetic rather than indiscipline. Its real counter-argument is that this excuses a professional failure by reframing it as a systems problem: confidentiality is the condition on which complainants participate at all, nobody accepts 'I was busy' as a reason to discuss a case in a lift, and — sharper — treating it as arithmetic invites management to accept the framing and keep the arithmetic, eroding the standard without anyone deciding to lower it. The write-up must say WHAT CHANGES ON MONDAY under their reading, because the two readings produce different first actions: explanation means ask without penalty and make the permitted path cheap; excuse means enforce and let the backlog become visible. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade prediction accuracy, grade the account of the gap.

opening.label: Predicted — % of your ER team who have used AI on case-related work
opening.hint: A summary, a chronology, a draft, a policy question with facts attached. Whole percent.

calibration.label: Actual — what you found when you asked, without penalty
calibration.hint: The benchmark for comparison is 70% of ER teams having used or trialled AI in 2025.

dimensions.name: No case facts, and the matter type is a type
dimensions.criteria: First a compliance check: the submission must contain no names, initials, incident dates, paraphrased allegations, or identifying descriptions. Flag any breach at the top and request resubmission without grading substance. Then the scope: the learner must have chosen a matter TYPE they own end to end, not a case and not a whole function. Credit a type specific enough that later modules can attach to it — 'harassment intake' or 'grievances at step two' rather than 'employee relations'.

dimensions.name: The rung mapping is granular where it matters
dimensions.criteria: Work products placed on rungs, with documents that span rungs broken down by section rather than assigned a single rung. The graded insight is identifying a place where the grammar of a sentence or section suggests one rung and its content does another — a characterization presented as an observation is the archetype, and a learner who found one in their own template should score at the top. Credit recognizing that applying a standard of proof is itself weighing, and therefore rung four.

dimensions.name: They actually asked, and reported honestly
dimensions.criteria: The AI-use map must show evidence of asking rather than assuming — how the question was framed matters, and framing it without penalty is the graded behaviour, because an audit that punishes disclosure returns a clean answer and no information. Credit entries with the rung, the tool, whether it was approved, and whether case content was involved. Credit 'I don't know' and credit reporting something the learner did not expect. A claim of zero use with no evidence of having asked should be pushed on against the benchmark that 70% of ER teams used or trialled AI in 2025.

dimensions.name: The one rule can be applied to a sentence
dimensions.criteria: The test is operational: could a colleague hold this rule up against a single sentence in a document and get an answer? 'AI may establish what exists and may never weigh it' passes. 'AI may assist with drafting but not decisions', 'use AI responsibly', or anything requiring the learner's own judgement to apply, fails — the module's whole argument is that the rung boundary rather than the task is the control, precisely because a summary can sit on any rung. Credit brevity; a rule longer than two sentences is a policy and will not be used.

dimensions.name: The delta and the position
dimensions.criteria: Predicted share of team AI use against what asking revealed, with an account of the gap — an undercount is the common and intended finding, and a learner whose team told them something surprising should be credited for having created the conditions where that was possible. Accuracy is never graded. Plus a committed position on the module's claim engaging the real counter-argument: that the arithmetic framing excuses a professional failure, that confidentiality is the condition of participation rather than a preference to trade against workload, and that accepting the framing lets management keep the arithmetic. The write-up MUST say what changes on Monday under their reading — the two readings produce different first actions, and a position that does not resolve to an action has not engaged the argument.
